name: NCD holding reward minted on the sender's current balance, farmed through pre-registered helpers
summary: NCD's _transfer mints the sender 1.5% of its current balance per full day since its mineStartTime on every non-pair transfer, so tokens moved into an address registered a day earlier earn a full day's reward at once. The attacker registered 100 helper contracts by skimming dust from the NCD/USDT pair, a day later bought NCD and passed it through every helper, compounding the reward 200 times, then sold the minted NCD to the pair through fresh contracts to dodge the 5%-of-balance and once-a-day sell limits.
notes: The seed's anchor 0xbfb9b3b8 (0xd52f1250) is the second exploit: 0xb9596d6e ran the same 200-mint helper chain 8,177 blocks earlier, against helpers it registered in 0x32bb6261 a day before. Every NCD reward mint since deployment was scanned: the four 200-mint transactions listed are the only ones that drained USDT; six earlier 100-mint transactions minted nothing, and the single-mint transactions are holder rewards.

Loss is the NCD/USDT pair's USDT outflow in the four transactions; the minted NCD is not counted. The creator's setSellmaxrate calls toggled the sell cap between 0 and 5, its value at deployment, before the exploit, and ownership was renounced at block 39235670, so the deployment is the reset.
